mainTopic: Whether רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's inheritance rule applies to a בריא, and whether the כתובה clause for sons proves it
overview: The amud opens with the end of רבא's instruction: a דיין rules only by what he himself understands. Then רבא asks a new question. Does רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's rule, that a father may direct his ירושה to one son, work only for a שכיב מרע, or also for a healthy man (בריא)? רב משרשיא answers from the כתובה clause in which a wife's sons 'will inherit' her כתובה money on top of their share. רבי at first says the wording is 'יסבון' (they will take). He later takes that back and proves that the wording is 'ירתון' (they will inherit). Since a healthy man writes the כתובה at his wedding, this seems to show that רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's rule works even for a בריא. רב פפא pushes back: nobody can transfer to sons who are not born yet, so the clause must work only because it is a תנאי בית דין, and it proves nothing. אביי first defends the proof from the word 'ירתון'. Then he retracts, because the daughters' clause next to it works like a gift, and in a case of 'gift to one, inheritance to another' even the רבנן agree. The amud ends as רב נחומי (or רב חנניה בר מניומי) begins a response to אביי, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A judge rules only by what he himself sees
steps.stepSummary: רבא finishes his instruction: do not learn from his ruling either, because a דיין must rule by his own understanding.
steps.simpleTranslation: But do not learn from it either, because a judge only has what his own eyes see.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a statement of רבא from just before this line. He tells his students not to learn from his ruling, because each judge must decide by his own understanding.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the second half of a two-part instruction. A judge may not lean on someone else's decision if he himself sees it differently. He must judge by what he actually sees and understands in the case.

keyTerms.meaning: What his eyes see, meaning his own understanding of the case

steps.whatToRemember: A דיין decides by his own understanding, not by copying another judge's ruling.

phrases.english: but do not learn from it either,
phrases.notes: "It" is a ruling of רבא that his students think has a mistake in it.

phrases.aramaic: דְּאֵין לַדַּיָּין אֶלָּא מַה שֶּׁעֵינָיו רוֹאוֹת.
phrases.english: as a judge has only what his eyes see.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes רבא's instruction from the end of the previous daf.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A judge must rule only by his own understanding of the case, not by another judge's ruling.

steps.title: Does the rule apply to a healthy man too?
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks whether רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's rule works only for a שכיב מרע, or also for a בריא.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא asked: what about a healthy person? When רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה said a father can leave his estate to one son, did he mean only a dying man, who is able to pass on an inheritance? Then a healthy man could not. Or perhaps even a healthy man can?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא opens a new topic with a question. He asks whether רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's rule is limited to a man on his deathbed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה lets a father choose which son inherits. One side of the question says only a שכיב מרע can do this, since passing on a ירושה happens at the time of death. The other side says a healthy man has the same power.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked (a real question he wants solved)
Able to pass on an inheritance

steps.confusionAlert: רבא is not asking whether a healthy man can give a gift (מתנה). He is asking whether he can use the language of inheritance (ירושה) to change who inherits.

phrases.english: Rava asks: with a healthy person, how is it?

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָאָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה –
phrases.english: When Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka said his rule,
phrases.notes: His rule is that a father may leave his inheritance to one of his sons.

phrases.english: was it about a person on his deathbed, since he is able to pass on an inheritance;
but with a healthy person, no;
or perhaps even with a healthy person as well?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new question, separate from the previous step.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's rule allowing a father to direct his ירושה applies only to a שכיב מרע or also to a בריא.

steps.title: A proof from the כתובה clause about sons
steps.stepSummary: רב משרשיא cites רבי נתן, who said a משנה about the כתובה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב משרשיא said to רבא: Come and hear. רבי נתן said to רבי: You taught your משנה according to רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה! As we learned: If a husband did not write for his wife, 'The sons you will have from me will inherit the money of your כתובה in addition to their share with their brothers,' he is still obligated, because it is a condition set by the court.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא tries to answer רבא's question. He brings רבי נתן's claim that a משנה about the כתובה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this clause, a husband makes his wife's sons 'inherit' extra money beyond their brothers' share. That is just what רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה allows. The husband sets this up when he marries, while he is healthy. So if this משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, his rule would work even for a בריא.

keyTerms.meaning: Marriage contract, which promises the wife money
A condition set by the court, which applies even if it was not written

steps.whyThisMatters: The proof depends on the exact word 'ירתון' (inherit). The next step argues over exactly that word.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא לְרָבָא: תָּא שְׁמַע,
phrases.english: Rav Mesharshiyya said to Rava: Come and hear,
as Rabbi Natan said to Rabbi:
phrases.notes: "רבי" with no name means רבי יהודה הנשיא, who put together the משנה.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁנִיתֶם מִשְׁנַתְכֶם כְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן בֶּן בְּרוֹקָה!
phrases.english: You taught your Mishna in accordance with Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka!
As we learned: If he did not write for her,
phrases.notes: This משנה is in כתובות נב:.

phrases.english: "Male children that you will have from me
will inherit the money of your marriage contract
in addition to their portion that they have with their brothers" —
he is obligated, as it is a stipulation of the court.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב מְשַׁרְשְׁיָא לְרָבָא: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to answer רבא's question from step 2.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's rule applies even to a בריא.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי נתן's claim that the כתובה clause 'ירתון' (sons will inherit extra) follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. The clause is set up by a healthy husband at marriage.

steps.title: רבי corrects the wording: 'they will take'
steps.stepSummary: רבי answers רבי נתן that the משנה's real wording is 'יסבון' (they will take), not 'ירתון' (they will inherit).
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי said to him: We learned 'they will take.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי rejects רבי נתן's claim by correcting the wording of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With the word 'יסבון', the sons receive the money as a kind of gift, not as ירושה. A gift is valid no matter whose opinion we follow, so the משנה does not need to follow רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. The next step shows that רבי himself later takes this answer back.

keyTerms.meaning: They will take (receive as a gift, not as inheritance)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי is not arguing about whether the sons get the money. They get it either way. He is only arguing about whether it comes as ירושה or as something like a מתנה.

phrases.english: And Rabbi said to him: We learned "they will take."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי נתן's reading, which was the basis of רב משרשיא's proof.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the claim that the כתובה משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The wording is 'יסבון' (take, like a gift), not 'ירתון' (inherit). So the clause works for everyone and needs no special inheritance rule.

steps.title: רבי takes back his reply and proves the wording is 'they will inherit'
steps.stepSummary: רבי admits he was too quick to argue with רבי נתן. He proves the משנה says 'ירתון', because the sons do not collect from sold property, and that only makes sense for an inheritance.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי said: I was young and immature, and I was brazen toward רבי נתן הבבלי. Since we hold that the sons' כתובה clause does not collect from sold property: if the משנה said 'they will take', why can't they collect from sold property? So it must say 'they will inherit'.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי cancels his own rejection from Step 4 and brings back רבי נתן's proof. He shows from a known הלכה that the משנה must say 'ירתון'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the sons got the money as a gift ('they will take'), their right would start at the wedding, before any later sale, so they could collect even from property the father sold afterward. But the הלכה is that they cannot collect from sold property. That fits only an inheritance, which comes only from what the father still owns when he dies.

keyTerms.meaning: I was brazen, I spoke with too much boldness
male children. This is the כתובה clause giving a wife's sons her כתובה money
collects from property that was sold to others, which is liened property

steps.confusionAlert: Step 4's דחיה is now cancelled. רבי himself goes back to agreeing with רבי נתן, so the proof for רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה stands again.

phrases.english: And Rabbi said:
There was immaturity in me
and I was brazen toward Natan the Babylonian
For since we hold:
the 'male children' clause does not collect from sold property
if you thought we learned 'they will take',
why does it not collect from sold property?
phrases.notes: A gift given at the wedding would come before any later sale, so it should be able to collect from it.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from this: we learned 'they will inherit'.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Cancels Step 4's rejection and restores Step 3's proof.
steps.raayaObject: That the משנה reads 'ירתון', which is inheritance language.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The accepted הלכה that the בנין דכרין clause does not collect from sold property.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A gift reading cannot explain why the sons cannot collect from sold property.

steps.title: The משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה, even for a healthy person
steps.stepSummary: Only רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה holds that a person can add to one heir's inheritance. Since a כתובה is written by a healthy man, his rule works even for a בריא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whom have you heard who holds this reasoning? רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. And learn from this that it applies even to a healthy person.
steps.whatsHappening: רב משרשיא's proof is completed, and it answers רבא's question from Step 2.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A clause that gives one wife's sons more of the estate adds to the inheritance of some heirs. That is רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's opinion. A man writes a כתובה when he marries, while healthy, so his rule is not limited to a שכיב מרע.

keyTerms.meaning: a healthy person, the opposite of a שכיב מרע
learn from this, conclude from it

steps.whatToRemember: The conclusion so far is that רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's rule works even for a בריא, because the כתובה clause for sons follows his view.

phrases.english: Whom have you heard
who holds this reasoning?
phrases.notes: He means the idea that a father can make one set of sons inherit more than the others.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan ben Beroka,
and learn from this: even with a healthy person.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן שָׁמְעַתְּ לֵיהּ דְּאִית לֵיהּ הַאי סְבָרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the reading established in Step 5.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's rule applies even to a בריא.

steps.title: רב פפא asks how anyone can transfer to unborn children
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא challenges the proof. Whichever way you read the משנה, a person cannot transfer ownership of something that has not come into the world.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: whether you say 'they will take' or 'they will inherit', a person cannot transfer ownership of something that has not come into the world!
steps.whatsHappening: A new attack begins. רב פפא questions whether the כתובה clause can work at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the כתובה is written, the sons who will receive the money are not born yet. So how can the husband give them any rights? If the clause itself cannot work, it is hard to use it as proof for רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.

keyTerms.meaning: something that has not yet come into the world
whether... or. The question works either way

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
Whether according to the one who says 'they will take',
or according to the one who says 'they will inherit',
a person cannot transfer ownership of
something that has not come into the world!
phrases.notes: The sons in the כתובה are not born yet when it is written.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב פָּפָּא לְאַבָּיֵי: בֵּין לְמַאן דְּאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the basis of the proof completed in Step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: Whether the בנין דכרין clause can work at all, and so whether it can prove anything about רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The receivers do not exist yet, and a person cannot transfer to what has not come into the world. This is true under both readings.

steps.title: Even רבי מאיר does not allow giving to someone not yet born
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא makes his challenge stronger. Even רבי מאיר only allows transferring a not-yet-existing item to an existing person. He does not allow transferring to a person who does not exist yet.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even according to רבי מאיר, who says a person can transfer something that has not come into the world, that is only to someone who exists. To someone who does not exist, no!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא closes off a possible answer. He shows that even the most lenient opinion does not help here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר allows a transfer when the thing being given is not here yet. Here the problem is different, because the person receiving it is not here yet. Nobody allows that, so the challenge applies according to all opinions.

keyTerms.meaning: someone or something that already exists in the world

steps.confusionAlert: Keep the two problems apart: giving an item that does not exist yet, which רבי מאיר allows, and giving to a person who does not exist yet, which nobody allows.

phrases.english: And even according to Rabbi Meir, who says:

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם מַקְנֶה דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא בָּא לָעוֹלָם,
phrases.english: a person can transfer something that has not come into the world,
that applies only to one who is in the world,
but to one who is not in the world, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens Step 7's challenge so that it works according to all opinions.
steps.kashyaTarget: A possible answer that relies on רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר's leniency covers an item that does not exist yet. It does not cover a receiver who does not exist yet, which is the problem with unborn sons.

steps.title: The clause for future sons is a special court rule
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא concludes that the כתובה clause works only because it is a תנאי בית דין. So it cannot prove anything about רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, a rule set up by the court is different. Here too, a rule set up by the court is different!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא finishes his attack on the proof from step 6. He says the כתובה clause is a special rule made by בית דין, so the normal limits on transferring property do not apply to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 7-8 showed that no opinion lets a person transfer anything to someone who is not born yet. The only way the clause for unborn sons can work is that חכמים made it a special court rule. If it is a special rule, it says nothing about whether a person may normally add to one heir's share. So the proof that the משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה falls away.

keyTerms.meaning: A condition set by the court; a rule חכמים built into every כתובה
Is different; follows its own special rules
Here too; the same is true in this case

phrases.english: Rather, a stipulation of the court is different;

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא נָמֵי – תְּנַאי בֵּית דִּין שָׁאנֵי!
phrases.english: here too, a stipulation of the court is different!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב פפא's challenge from steps 7-8 by stating where it leads: the כתובה clause is a special court rule.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof in step 6 that the משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The כתובה clause is a תנאי בית דין, which has its own special power, so it cannot show the normal law of inheritance.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a rule made by בית דין can do things a private person's transfer cannot do. So you cannot learn the regular law from it.

steps.title: The proof comes from the word 'they will inherit'
steps.stepSummary: אביי defends the proof: the משנה uses the language of inheritance, 'ירתון', and that points to רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The proof is because the clause is phrased with the word 'they will inherit.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב פפא. Even if the clause is a court rule, the fact that it is written as an inheritance still shows the משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי moves the proof away from the question of how the transfer works. He puts it on the wording instead. Since בית דין chose to word the clause as 'ירתון', it seems a person really can direct his inheritance to particular heirs. That is רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה's view.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is אביי answering רב פפא.

phrases.english: Because it expresses it
with the wording 'they will inherit.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא מַפֵּיק לַהּ בִּלְשׁוֹן יִרְתוּן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's rejection by basing the proof on the wording of the clause.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Moves the proof onto the wording
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the clause is a court rule, it proves nothing about רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The court still chose inheritance language, 'ירתון', and that matches רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.

steps.title: אביי takes back his answer and points to the daughters' clause
steps.stepSummary: אביי says his answer was wrong. He brings the next clause in the משנה: even if not written, the husband must support his future daughters from his property until they marry, because it is a תנאי בית דין.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי then said: What I said is not correct. As we learned in the משנה: if he did not write for her, 'The daughters you will have from me will live in my house and be fed from my property until they marry', he is still obligated, because it is a condition of the court.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי takes back his own defense. He brings the clause in the כתובה about daughters, which sits right next to the clause about sons. The next step uses it to explain why the word 'ירתון' proves nothing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daughters' clause gives the daughters support from the estate. That is not an inheritance; it works like a gift. Because the sons' clause and the daughters' clause stand side by side, the two together set up a special case. The next step explains it.

keyTerms.meaning: Went back; then (said again, changing his mind)
It is not correct; it is nothing

phrases.english: Abaye then said:
What I said is not correct,
as we learned:
If he did not write for her:
'Female children that you will have from me'
will live in my house
and be fed from my property
until they are taken by husbands'
he is obligated,
because it is a stipulation of the court.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לָאו מִילְּתָא הִיא דַּאֲמַרִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: אביי retracts his own answer from step 10 and brings a source to set up why.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects אביי's own claim that the word 'ירתון' proves the משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The sons' clause sits next to the daughters' clause, which is like a gift. That changes how the word 'ירתון' should be read.

steps.title: A gift to one and an inheritance to another works for everyone
steps.stepSummary: The daughters get their support like a gift, and the sons get their share as an inheritance. In such a mixed case even the רבנן agree, so the word 'ירתון' does not prove the משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: So it is a case of 'to this one as a gift and to that one as an inheritance.' In any case of 'to this one as an inheritance and to that one as a gift,' even the רבנן agree.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his retraction. Because the כתובה gives to the daughters as a gift and to the sons as an inheritance, even the רבנן accept the word 'ירתון' here.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן normally argue with רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. But they agree that a gift to one person and an inheritance to another, given together, is valid. The כתובה's two clauses fit exactly that pattern. So the inheritance wording fits the רבנן too, and the proof for רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה falls away.
steps.whatToRemember: The word 'ירתון' in the כתובה does not prove the משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה. The sons' inheritance clause sits next to the daughters' gift-like support, and in a case of 'gift to one, inheritance to another' even the רבנן agree.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the daughters inherit. They only get food and housing until marriage, which is treated like a gift. The sons are the ones described with 'ירתון'.

phrases.english: And it is to this one as a gift
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the daughters, whose support is like a gift.

phrases.english: and to that one as an inheritance,
phrases.notes: 'That one' is the sons, who get their mother's כתובה money as an inheritance.

phrases.english: and in any case of 'to this one as an inheritance and to that one as a gift'
even the Rabbis agree.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains why the daughters' clause from step 11 cancels אביי's proof from the word 'ירתון'.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The inheritance wording in the כתובה fits even the רבנן. So the proof that the משנה follows רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה is rejected.
steps.whyThisMatters: It teaches the rule 'לזה במתנה ולזה בירושה', which even the רבנן accept. It also ends the attempt to tie this משנה to רבי יוחנן בן ברוקה.

steps.title: A new speaker turns to אביי
steps.stepSummary: רב נחומי, or according to others רב חנניה בר מניומי, begins to speak to אביי. This line only sets up the response that follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחומי (some say it was רב חנניה בר מניומי) said to אביי:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move: a new אמורא is about to respond to אביי's conclusion. His actual words come right after this line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: So far we only know who is speaking and who he is talking to, not what he says. The גמרא is unsure which of two אמוראים said this, so it gives both names. Because the line is spoken 'to אביי' right after אביי's conclusion, it is most likely opening a challenge to that conclusion.

keyTerms.meaning: And some say. Gives another opinion about who said the statement.
The first name given for the speaker.

steps.confusionAlert: There are not two people speaking here. It is one speaker, and the גמרא is just unsure of his name.

phrases.english: Rav Naḥumi said to him

phrases.aramaic: וְאִית דְּאָמַר רַב חֲנַנְיָה בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי, לְאַבָּיֵי:
phrases.english: and some say it was Rav Ḥananya bar Minyumi, to Abaye:

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נְחוּמִי וְאִית דְּאָמַר רַב חֲנַנְיָה בַּר מִנְיוֹמֵי, לְאַבָּיֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns to אביי right after his conclusion in step 12 and opens a response to it.
steps.kashyaTarget: אביי's conclusion in step 12. The content of the challenge appears in the following text.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Not yet stated. This line only gives the speaker and the person he is addressing.
